description:
pkix-path-builder/src/lib.rs:195-200 introduces the first struct-style variant on the public Error enum:

```rust
NoValidPath {
    tried: usize,
    last_error: alloc::string::String,
}
```

The Error enum carries #[non_exhaustive] at the enum level, which permits ADDING new variants in future versions without breaking callers (Rust API guideline C-EXHAUSTIVE). However, #[non_exhaustive] at the enum level does NOT extend to struct-variant fields — within a struct variant, the field set is exhaustive. A caller writing

```rust
Err(Error::NoValidPath { tried, last_error }) => ...
```

binds both fields by name; if the maintainer adds a third field later (e.g., a typed partial_chains: Vec<…>, a kind: NoValidPathKind disambiguator, or the typed pkix_path::Error that PKIX-wnnn.5 contemplates), every caller that destructures NoValidPath without `..` breaks. Adding `..` to existing match arms requires source-modification of every caller's match site — a breaking change under cargo-semver-checks.

This matters specifically because the existing PKIX-wnnn.5 finding suggests the maintainer should add a typed inner error in a future version. Combining that future change with "add a field to NoValidPath" forces a coordinated breaking change.

Two principled fixes:

1. Apply #[non_exhaustive] to the variant itself: `#[non_exhaustive] NoValidPath { tried, last_error }`. This forces all callers to use `..` from day one, preserving the maintainer's freedom to add fields. Cost: callers' destructuring patterns become slightly more verbose.

2. Wrap in a dedicated #[non_exhaustive] payload struct: `NoValidPath(NoValidPathDetails)` where `NoValidPathDetails` is its own #[non_exhaustive] struct with accessor methods. Callers cannot construct or exhaustively destructure NoValidPathDetails; they go through the API. Cost: an extra type and accessors.

Either approach is a one-time breaking change pre-1.0 that buys forever flexibility. Doing it AFTER 1.0 ships requires a 2.0 cut.

Note: The other Error variants are all unit variants (NoPathFound, DepthExceeded, BudgetExceeded, MalformedIntermediate) so they have no field-evolution concern. NoValidPath is the first struct variant; it's the natural place to set the pattern.

Bears on AGENTS.md non-negotiable #6 (cache-friendly result types — serde format evolution depends on field stability) and on the prelaunch framing: breaking changes are free pre-1.0; "design for the eventual complete shape."
title: Error::NoValidPath struct-variant fields are exhaustive — adding fields later is a breaking change
